summary: Red team of the KW II extraction (Khare–Wintenberger, Serre's modularity conjecture (II), Invent. Math. 178 (2009) 505–586), read in the authors' copy (hash matches). The item-level work is careful. The locators are right, the library citations hold at the pins, and 31 of the 32 recorded source issues are real, with the review's rejection of E13 correct. The trouble is in routing and in how far the planned statuses reach at p = 2. There are 16 findings: 10 medium and 6 low. (1) The routes create dependency cycles. Theorems 8.2 and 8.4 go to R20.6, but their inputs go downstream of it: Lemma 7.10, the character ψ and Kisin's level raising to GL2ModularityLifting R22.1/R22.4, which require R20.6; Khare's Lemma 2.2 to R23.3, which imports Theorem 8.2. (2) Grunwald–Wang, and the square-root lemma, go to IG.4, while three accepted extractions route the same theorem to ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4. (3) The §4 presentations are planned at R04.3 nodes restricted to p > 2, and Lemma 4.4(2) has no node. (4) The p = 2 local points in Taylor's moduli problem (Theorem 6.1) have no item, and the Taylor nodes are odd-l only. (5) A missed source error: §3.2.4 applies Savitt's non-smooth ring when k(ρ̄_p) = 2, where the ring is the smooth crystalline one. (6) The §3.2.3 smoothness at k = p and p = 2 has no supplier. (7) Four planned items are stated by no node; one of these nodes (the p = 2 patching datum) is wrong. (8) Kisin's Corollary 3.1.11 is misstated: its level-raising congruence hypothesis is missing. (9) KW I Theorem 4.1 is planned at a node whose proof uses only Theorem 9.7, which cannot give the potentially Barsotti–Tate or k = p + 1, k(ρ̄) = 2 cases. (10) Two missing items are partly planned (ModularCurves 4D, ProfiniteCohomology layer 9) or partly in the library (TauCeti.kummerMap). Low: duplicate stage routing of the Jacobson facts; the owner of SL₂(𝔽_{2^r}) cohomology; two definitions without items; wrong details in E8 and E17; nodes that do not allow KW's non-compact levels at p = 2; two inaccurate notes.

Source. Authors' copy https://www.math.ucla.edu/~shekhar/papers/proofs.pdf, fetched 30 September 2026 (TLS chain incomplete, so fetched without certificate verification; the hash covers this). 98 pp., SHA-256 53f45f8be3b3c7de19f42417920d34a809e908412826490ebed90f07c8e86ed4, which matches the recorded hash. The Springer version of record was not read; findings that quote the paper are scoped to this copy.

Reading. The whole paper was read in a text extraction, pp. 1–98 (§§1–10 and references [1]–[69]), divided by section among parallel readers. Every finding filed here was re-checked personally at its locator. P. 39 was rendered at 250 dpi and confirms the review's rejection of E13: the bar on R̄^{□,ψ}_v in the second bullet of §4.1.3 is printed as a wide overline.

Items. All 340 items were checked against the text: statement, hypotheses (p odd against p = 2, ℚ_p against unramified F_v, totally real F, compact against non-compact levels) and locator. For planned items, every node or stage named in the note was opened and read. Problems found are reported in findings 3–9 and 13–15; the rest hold.

Key theorems read against their planned nodes: Theorem 3.1 and Propositions 3.2, 3.3, 3.6 (R08.1/R08.6), Proposition 4.1, 4.5, Corollary 4.7 and Lemmas 4.4, 4.6 (R04.3/R04.4/R04.6/R03.2), Lemma 5.10 and Proposition 5.11 (R04.5), Theorem 6.1(i)–(iii) (R23.3/R23.5 and the Taylor nodes of R23.2/R23.3), Lemmas 7.1–7.4, Corollaries 7.5 and 7.8, Definition 7.9 (R18.3, R19.4–R19.6, R22.2), Propositions 9.2, 9.3, Lemmas 9.4–9.6 and Theorem 9.7 (R22.3, R22.5, R22.6), Theorem 10.1 (R24.1), §10.2 (R24.4, R22.5, R21.4/R21.5, R32.2), §10.3 (R24.3, R24.5, R19.5).

Library claims. All twelve declarations of the seven library items were opened at the pins and hold: Mathlib 082e2d3 cyclotomicCharacter (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/CyclotomicCharacter.lean:307) and modularCyclotomicCharacter; CategoryTheory.Coyoneda.fullyFaithful and Functor.CorepresentableBy; PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassDivision (Mathlib/RingTheory/PowerSeries/WeierstrassPreparation.lean:504) and exists_isWeierstrassFactorization; groupCohomology.H1InfRes and H1InfRes_exact (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/GroupCohomology/Functoriality.lean:365, 393); Subgroup.relIndex_dvd_index_of_normal (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Index.lean:154) and Subgroup.Normal.subgroupOf; HenselianLocalRing (Mathlib/RingTheory/Henselian.lean:108, with IsAdicComplete.henselianRing at :170); Tau Ceti f790474 Representation.nonempty_equiv_of_character_eq and FDRep.nonempty_iso_of_character_eq (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/CharacterTable/Determined.lean:72, 115; [CharZero k], which matches characteristic 0).

Missing items. All 29 were searched for in every packet node, packet request, reserved id, new roadmap, atlas stage text and the declaration index at the pins (Mathlib and Tau Ceti). Findings 7, 10, 11 and 12 report the ones whose status or owner is wrong. The rest are correctly missing, for example Theorems 8.2, 8.4, Lemma 8.3, Lemma 7.10, Kisin 3.1.11 and Taylor's neatness lemma, none of which any node states. Searched for planned items already in the libraries (Schlessinger, Chebotarev, Brauer induction, Dickson, Poitou–Tate, Tate duality, Jacquet–Langlands, strong approximation, Moret-Bailly, Krull height, Auslander–Buchsbaum, Teichmüller): none is at the pins in the form the items need.

Routes. The eleven route stages were read, and the whole stage chain R20.1–R20.6 → R22.1 → … → R22.6, R23.1–R23.6 and R24.1 was followed (finding 1). Every other accepted paper extraction was searched for the same mathematics: Grunwald–Wang, square roots of characters, Khare's Lemma 4.2, Taylor neatness, Jacobson and regularity facts, Kummer theory and SL₂ cohomology. The overlaps found are findings 2, 10, 11 and 12. No extraction of Kisin 2009 or Taylor 2002 exists in the atlas. KW I and BCDT route no KW II item to a different owner.

Source issues. All 32 were checked at their locators. E11 was re-derived: for q ≡ 1 mod 4 a level-2 character of 2-power order has ε^{q+1} ≠ 1, and the corrected eigenvalue ε^q works. E19 was re-derived: γ and γη have the same residual eigenvalue set exactly when N(v) ≡ −1 mod p. E29 was re-derived: points with a semistable condition at ℓ ≠ p stay ramified over every finite extension, and the mod-p correction works. E14, E17 and E13 (rejected) were checked on the text and page image. E8 and E17 have wrong details (finding 14). One missed source error was found: §3.2.4 at k(ρ̄) = 2 (finding 5).
Review changes. The review changed only the 32 verdicts and the report's count. Its rejection of E13 is correct (page image), and its confirmations of the other 31 hold, subject to finding 14.

findings.claim: At p = 2 no node states KW's presentation machinery, although these items are planned there for all p. The nodes they cite, R04.3/relative-tangent-space and R04.3/local-to-global-presentation, are stated under 'p > 2' in Gee's conventions. They use ad⁰ρ̄ with dual module ad⁰ρ̄(1), and they frame only finite places. KW need three things these nodes lack. (a) The correction δ_p, with the tangent space equal to the η-image, of dimension h¹ − δ_p. (b) The dual (Ad⁰)*(1) ≅ Ad/Z, which is not ad⁰(1) at p = 2. (c) Framed infinite places. The p = 2 case matters: Proposition 4.5 and Corollary 4.7 at p = 2 give the 2-adic lifts of KW I Theorem 5.1. Only the decomposition node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.2/presentation-relations-and-dual-selmer-bound says 'KW II treats all p', and /143, /150, /151 and /153 do not cite it. /144 (Lemma 4.4(2): the generator count with determinant fixed only on S and Ad coefficients) is needed only at p = 2, for Lemma 5.10(e). No node states it: R04.4/determinant-fixed-on-S only defines the ring, and R04.5/dyadic-taylor-wiles-primes says '(e) follows by Lemma 4.4'.

Its statement uses 'H¹_{S,T}(G_{F,S}, ad⁰ρ̄) … h¹_{S,T}(ad⁰(1))'. Paper p. 39: 'Note that (Ad⁰)* = Hom_𝔽(Ad⁰, 𝔽) is isomorphic to Ad/Z … The G_F-module Ad/Z is isomorphic to Ad⁰ when p > 2, and need not be so when p = 2.' Paper p. 41, Lemma 4.4(1): '… dim_𝔽(H¹_{{L_v}}(S∪V, Ad⁰)) − δ_p + …'. Paper p. 41, proof of Lemma 4.4: 'We prove only 1. as 2. is similar.' findings.claim: §3.2.4 applies Savitt's ring 𝒪[[T₁,T₂]]/(T₁T₂ − p) to every irreducible ρ̄_p with p odd. That is wrong when k(ρ̄_p) = 2. The weight-two type is then (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) = (1 ⊕ 1, 0), the trivial type. Take for example ρ̄_p|I_p ≅ ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^p, which is E[p] for a supersingular E. The lifts of this type are the crystalline weight-2 lifts of §3.2.3, whose ring is formally smooth, 𝒪[[T]]. Savitt's irreducible case needs a principal-series type ω̃^i ⊕ ω̃^j with i ≢ j, as the atlas node R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings states. 𝒪[[T]] is not isomorphic to 𝒪[[T₁,T₂]]/(T₁T₂ − p): their special fibres 𝔽[[T]] and 𝔽[[T₁,T₂]]/(T₁T₂) differ, the first being regular and the second not. Theorem 3.1 is unaffected, since both rings are flat domains of relative dimension 1 with regular generic fibre. But items /92 and /93, and the R08.6 export node, state the wrong ring when k(ρ̄_p) = 2. The extraction did not record this.
findings.evidence: Paper p. 23, §3.2.2(i): 'the lifts ρ_v are potentially semistable of weight 2 … with inertial Weil-Deligne parameter (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0) if k(ρ̄_v) ≠ p + 1'. Paper p. 24, §3.2.4: 'We suppose p ≠ 2 … Savitt proved that … this ring is isomorphic to O[[T1, T2]]/(T1T2 − p) (3 of th. 6.22 of [54]).' Paper p. 24, §3.2.3: 'We suppose that the representation ρ̄_p … is irreducible of weight k ≤ p and we consider lifts that are crystalline of weight k. The deformation ring is smooth over O of dimension 1'. Node LocalGaloisDeformationRings:R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings: '(1) If τ = ω̃^i ⊕ ω̃^j with i ≢ j mod p − 1: … 𝒪_E⟦X₁, X₂⟧/(X₁X₂ − pw) … in the irreducible case'. Node R08.6/export-weight-two-irreducible: '… is 𝒪⟦T₁, T₂⟧/(T₁T₂ − p) … and it is not formally smooth', with no restriction on k(ρ̄_p).
findings.fix: Add the hypothesis 3 ≤ k(ρ̄_p) ≤ p to /92 and /93. Note that for k(ρ̄_p) = 2 the weight-two ring is the formally smooth crystalline ring of §3.2.3 (/91). Record a sourceIssue: kind error, locator §3.2.4 p. 24, affects nothing, since Theorem 3.1's properties still hold. Send LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 a request to restrict export-weight-two-irreducible in the same way.

L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition works in the Fontaine–Laffaille category with Fil^{l−1}M = 0, which gives Hodge–Tate weights in [0, p − 2]. Weight k means weights {0, k − 1}, so the node covers k ≤ p − 1 only, and for p = 2 it is empty. R08.6/export-fontaine-laffaille-irreducible asserts 'the same holds for p = 2 (k = 2)' with L7 as its only input. The paper gives no argument either. It says the published argument excludes these cases and 'extends'. So the item is planned for k ≤ p − 1, p odd, only.

findings.claim: Item /273 misstates Kisin's Corollary 3.1.11. It gives the corollary's hypothesis as 'the p-torsion of the cokernel of the degeneracy map … has only Eisenstein maximal ideals in its support'. That is the Ihara-type input, which is Kisin's Lemma 3.1.8 and KW's Lemma 7.1. The corollary's actual hypotheses are these: a non-Eisenstein m; S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)_m ≠ 0; the level-raising congruence T_λ² − ψ(λ)(N(λ) + 1)² ≡ 0 on S_{σ,ψ}(U, O) mod m; and the pairing and smallness set-up of §3.1, which KW secure with the U(r₀) level on p. 77. Its conclusion is that S(U′, O)_m / i(S(U, O)_m²) is a non-zero free O-module. In KW's application the congruence comes from the lifting data at the v_j, which is Kisin's Lemma 3.5.3(ii). The item omits it, so a builder working from /273 would drop the one hypothesis level raising needs.
findings.evidence: Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity, Ann. of Math. 170 (2009), p. 1151: 'COROLLARY (3.1.11). Let m ⊂ T^univ_{S_p,O} be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Suppose that S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)_m ≠ {0} and that (T_λ² − ψ(λ)(N(λ) + 1)²)(S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)) ⊂ m S_{σ,ψ}(U, O). Then the quotient S_{σ,ψ}(U′, O)_m / i(S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)²_m) is a non-zero free O-module.' Its proof: 'That the quotient is torsion-free follows from (3.1.8).' KW II p. 77: 'By Lemma 7.1 … the kernel of the reduction of this map … has only Eisenstein maximal ideals in its support. Then from Corollary 3.1.11 of [36] … there is an automorphic representation π_i … Steinberg at all places of F_i above {v_1, …, v_{i+1}}.'
findings.fix: Restate /273 with Kisin's hypotheses: non-Eisenstein m, S(U, O)_m ≠ 0, the level-raising congruence at the new place, and the pairing and neat-level set-up. State the conclusion, and name Lemma 7.1 (/222) as the Ihara input. Add Lemma 3.5.3's condition (ii) (inert/split tower) and say where KW obtain the congruence: ρ̄ unramified at v_j (Lemma 8.1), with lifting data (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v).

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II.result.json: items PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/313, PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-II/314 (planned at PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.4); node R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1
findings.claim: Items /313 and /314 are planned at R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1, which states all of KW I Theorem 4.1. Its proof, however, uses only Theorem 9.7 after an allowable base change: '(α), (β); allowable base change; Theorem 9.7 over F; descent to ℚ'. That cannot give all cases. Theorem 9.7 needs F unramified at p and lifts of type (A), (B) or (C), and (A) allows weight p + 1 only when k(ρ̄) = p + 1. A potentially Barsotti–Tate lift whose type needs a ramified extension at p never becomes (A)–(C) over such an F. Nor does a crystalline weight-(p + 1) lift with k(ρ̄) = 2. §10.2 takes these cases from the literature instead: Kisin [36] for potentially Barsotti–Tate, Kisin [38] with Berger–Li–Zhu for k = p + 1 non-ordinary, and Diamond [16], Wiles and Taylor–Wiles for the ordinary and semistable cases. The Remark on p. 92 says so. /314's note lists these citations, but the planned node's proof does not use them, so the planned status rests on a node whose proof fails for part of the statement.
findings.evidence: Paper p. 92: 'Theorem 4.1 (2) (ii) is proved by Kisin in [36] in the potentially Barsotti-Tate case. The semistable weight 2 case goes back to [66] and [64], and [16]. Thus we need only prove 4.1(1) and 4.1 (2)(i), and the latter only when k = p.' Remark, p. 92: 'The arguments here in fact treat in a self-contained manner all cases of Theorem 4.1(2)(i) except k = p + 1 with k(ρ̄) = 2, and treats 4.1(2)(ii) when ρ|Q_p(μ_p) is semistable weight 2.' Paper p. 89, Theorem 9.7: 'Let F be a totally real field unramified at p …'. Paper p. 75, (A): 'with the case k = p + 1 considered only when F is split at p and k(ρ̄) = p + 1'. Node R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1, proof steps: 'Residual inputs (α), (β).', 'Allowable base change F/ℚ …', 'Theorem 9.7 over F.', 'Descent to ℚ.'
findings.fix: In /313 and /314, split the planned coverage by case. (2)(ii) potentially Barsotti–Tate goes to GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting. (2)(ii) potentially semistable but not potentially crystalline reduces by a finite-order twist to the semistable case (/318). k = p + 1 with k(ρ̄) = 2 goes to GL2ModularityLifting:R32.2/odd-prime-de-rham-lifting with OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting:R21.5/blz-reduction-theorem.
